correctness.rationale: For the randomized probability integral transform, conditional expectation given \(X\) is the mid-distribution value \(M\), and total variance gives \(\operatorname{Var}(M)=(1-S_3)/12\). Exchangeability gives \(\Delta=4\operatorname{Cov}(X,M)\); Cauchy--Schwarz yields the inequality and its equality condition forces \(X\) to be affine in \(M\). Convexity gives the support-cardinality bound. For two iid draws, \(YZ=X_1X_2\) and \(Y+Z=X_1+X_2\); under reflection symmetry these identities give the stated correlation transform. I independently checked the inequality and equality construction on exact rational examples, and the frozen exact-rational verifier was read.
correctness.risk: The order-statistic corollary requires reflection symmetry outside the equal-mass special case.

originality.rationale: The decisive ingredients are already standard and published: the mid-distribution literature gives \(E[M]=1/2\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(M)=(1-\sum p_i^3)/12\), while the Gini methodology expresses Gini mean difference as covariance with rank; the discrete midrank version follows directly from the same pairwise-sign identity. The submitted inequality and support equality condition are then exactly one Cauchy--Schwarz step and its equality criterion. Papadatos already gives the equal-mass min--max constant and arithmetic-progression equality case. Thus the package is a clean synthesis, but under implication-based originality the main theorem is covered by established identities plus routine linear-algebraic inequality.

final_claim: For a finite discrete law with masses \(p_i\), Gini mean difference \(\Delta\), variance \(\sigma^2\), and \(S_3=\sum_i p_i^3\), one has \(\Delta^2\le \frac43(1-S_3)\sigma^2\), with equality exactly when the support is a positive affine image of the mid-distribution values; the corresponding cardinality and reflection-symmetric two-sample min--max correlation bounds are sharp.
limitations: Finite discrete distributions for the cubic atom formula.
The min--max corollary is restricted to reflection-symmetric profiles/supports.
This rejection is for implication/value, not correctness.
